context:
Goal: controls in your apps feel substantial.
Problem (goal): the UX house rules say nothing about haptics, so no designer or reviewer asks for them.
Based on (read): docs/design/principles.md has no haptics rule; no file in docs/design or the iOS skill mentions haptics.
Departs from: main (no haptics rule) — adds a house rule and its checklist line.

Asked and answered in chat with triage. Your words, Nov 1 12:18 CST: "apps should consider integrating haptics on things like sliders to make it feel substantial". Filed as roadmap step ux-haptics-rule.

lastAnswer.note: apps should consider integrating haptics on things like sliders to make it feel substantial

options.gain: Designers and reviewers ask for haptics on sliders and similar controls.
options.how: A new rule in docs/design/principles.md and a line in checklist.md.
options.label: Add a haptics house rule
options.lose: One more line on each screen's checklist.

title: Should the UX house rules ask apps to consider haptics on controls like sliders?
